text: PART A, the load-bearing transfer: sigmoid ALREADY MEASURED the failure mode I was about to walk into, on this exact GPU. Selection-based sparse attention loses below ~8-16k positions because the GATHER dominates the attention (2.58 ms gather vs 0.82 ms attention at 65536). Consequence for R5: the coarse level must be built by a STRIDED MEAN POOL that the kernel reads with computed offsets, never by index_select/gather of selected blocks. A mean pool is a contiguous reduction with no materialised selection. This is the single reason the mechanism can be cheap where the dyadic schedule was 53x. ROLLBACK: none needed, it is a design constraint not a change.

R2's framing needs correcting: APPNP is NOT the similarity baseline. Decidable criterion -- a similarity weighting is pairwise, so a third token's perturbation cannot move the RATIO of two weights in a row. Measured: softmax attention ratio 0.376137914 -> 0.376137914 (invariant to 9 digits); APPNP influence ratio 0.787332 -> 0.808386 (2.7% move); max-plus influence moved 9.0000 with min entry still 0.000e+00. text: Context poisoning reproduced and fixed at the root. An out-of-range index_select on CUDA raises a device-side assert that is NOT recoverable in-process: every later CUDA test in the run failed with the same error even though their own inputs were valid (9 tests contaminated, measured). Fix is to clamp the gather index inside each pyramid level BEFORE adding the level base, in ceq/multizoom.py::multizoom_reference, and to clamp again inside the Triton kernel with tl.maximum(tl.minimum(rows, n_pool-1), 0). The mask already discards those rows so clamping changes no result. ROLLBACK: revert the two clamps; the cost is that any plan/tensor mismatch becomes an unrecoverable process-wide failure instead of a wrong-but-masked row.

detail: max abs diff 6.53 vs the CPU reference. text: R6's falsifier requires the module to flag a planted contradiction 'measurably more than an averaging baseline'. The sign is wrong: the averaging baseline wins. AUROC over 200 contradicted vs 200 clean draws, 40 nodes in two regions of 20, sigma=0.3 reading noise, one cross-region edge off by DELTA=2.0. Columns are LS-rms(averaging L2) / LS-max|r|(averaging Linf) / holonomy_z(module) / max-plus eigenvalue. chords=0 (5 cycles): 0.7741 0.7280 0.7068 0.6545. chords=12 (17): 0.8443 0.7774 0.8562 0.5839. chords=50 (53): 0.8671 0.8841 0.7870 0.7112. chords=150 (149): 0.8589 0.9860 0.9067 0.6841. chords=400 (386): 0.8017 0.9799 0.8918 0.6495. Pre-registered bar was AUROC>=0.90 AND gap>=+0.10; measured best cell is 0.9067 against 0.9860, gap -0.0793.

'Averaged away' is false as a premise. Least squares does not average a local contradiction away - fitting ONE global potential and reading the LARGEST single edge residual localises it to the edge that carries it, reaching 0.9860 at 149 cycles. The module and both averaging reads see the identical subspace (the cycle space = orthogonal complement of the image of the incidence map); they differ only in the norm, so R6 is a norm choice and not a mechanism.

COLLAPSE HYPOTHESIS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. The max cycle mean is the max-plus eigenvalue and the log of the Perron root - literally R3's contraction certificate read in the log domain - so if R3 and R6 were one mechanism it would be the detector. It is the WORST column at every cycle count tested: 0.6545, 0.5839, 0.7112, 0.6841, 0.6495. R3 and R6 do not collapse through the Perron root.

TRANSFERABLE, and the only thing that survives R6: the max-plus eigenvalue divides a cycle defect by cycle LENGTH because that is what makes it an eigenvalue; for DETECTION the denominator must be sqrt(length), because accumulated reading noise grows as sqrt(L) while a planted contradiction does not grow at all. Worth +0.2723 AUROC (0.5839 -> 0.8562 at 17 cycles). Also: build the fundamental cycle basis from a BFS tree, not insertion-order union-find - an arbitrary tree gives 39-edge cycles on a 40-node graph and the defect competes with sigma*sqrt(39).

WHY the sheaf died, stated precisely enough to be useful: a generic SO(d) holonomy fixes an axis iff d is odd, so on a COMPACT structure group the obstruction to a global section is generically invisible to a RANK statistic - dim ker was the wrong instrument, not the wrong subject. Moving to translations of the line (non-compact, fixes nothing) makes the obstruction a VALUE, generically nonzero on any graph with a cycle. That escape is real and measured here (test_the_statistic_is_zero_exactly_when_a_global_potential_exists, green, exact 0 vs >1e-3), and it still loses to least squares under noise.

R4's falsifier is passed by things that are not forgetting. Run literally it PASSES: effective size 2.3384/32, task-relevant held-out R2 0.97333, crushed-noise R2 -0.11446 (400 contexts, 300/100 split). The controls kill it. Same probe, same split, readout row: attention 1.0059/0.99947/-0.11579, row-stochastic 2.2887/0.98590/-0.11947, perron 2.3384/0.97333/-0.11446. A RETAINED filler token the gate did NOT crush reconstructs at -0.11224 vs the crushed one at -0.11446, gap +0.00222 against a pre-registered 0.25; the context mean scores -0.10015. The readout forgets everything equally. And standard attention passes every R4 clause outright at effective size 1.0059.

THEOREM, not a tuning problem: rho<1 is exactly the condition that makes I-A invertible, so a contraction-certified settling operator destroys nothing. Measured on the token axis: max|(I-A)Z - X| = 7.699e-14, smallest singular value of I-A = 0.011443, cond(I-A) = 767.8129, rho = 0.899482. The certificate R1 and R3 need is the same inequality that forbids R4, and a gate cannot change it - it scales columns of A, it cannot make I-A singular.

'Effective size' as a participation ratio is not a compression measurement. Settled state 2.2887 of 32 (a 14x apparent squeeze) from an input at 29.0164 of 32, and the map is a bijection. This is the same class of error Epsilon-Hollow flags in its own words about referenced_evictions=0: 'It is not a measurement. It is the only value the expression can produce.'

What DOES forget, measured: eviction, not gating. Setting a filler's salience to EXACTLY zero leaves its column of A exactly zero and the settled state STILL moves when that token is edited, through the softmax normaliser of every other row - zero weight is not absence. Removing the token from the key set (NeMo-Relay scope exit; foliation collapse of a free face, refcount 0 and no resident children) leaves the settled state BITWISE unchanged under any edit of the dropped token. At KEEP=16 of 96 with the matched-budget controls foliation's own sweep demands, task-relevant held-out R2 is salience 0.98687, random 0.18628, recency 0.04622. Genuine structural forgetting - and a rule applied from outside the operator, which R4's first sentence excludes.

At 876/2080 = 42.1% of dense blocks, matched budget, seq=2048. spread 0.05: random 0.3714, same-budget block oracle 0.6088, window+sinks 0.6738, MULTIZOOM 0.0003. spread 0.3: 0.3716 / 0.5885 / 0.6726 / 0.0095. spread 1.5: 0.4556 / 0.4609 / 0.6813 / 0.2964. text: The random->oracle AXIS IS UNDEFINED on this workload, and that is itself a result. The same-budget block-granular oracle scores WORSE than random (0.6088 vs 0.3714), so the axis denominator (err_random - err_oracle) is negative. Verified the oracle is genuine and not a bug: at full budget it reproduces dense to 2.5e-07 and its error falls monotonically with budget (0.6088 -> 0.2226 -> 0.0000 -> 0.0000 at 1x/2x/4x/8x). The cause is structural: one top-k choice is shared by all `block` queries in a query block, and those queries want different blocks. CONSEQUENCE: the 0.39-vs-0.975 axis scores on record are workload-specific and should not be treated as a universal ranking. Reported raw errors instead of a ratio.

ACCURACY BOUND HOLDS, and is informative exactly where the theory says it should be. ||A-A~||_inf <= (D_inf/2)(exp(delta_max)-1) + max_G[min(2, exp(R_G)-1)*r_G] with R_G = scale*||q||*diam(K_G) and delta_G <= R_G^2/8 by Hoeffding's lemma. Measured vs predicted over 6 seeds x 3 spreads, 0 violations. Non-vacuity (bound < trivial convex-hull range 4.79-6.91): spread 0.001 -> 1.67e-06 vs 9.58e-05 YES; 0.005 -> 9.00e-06 vs 2.42e-03 YES; 0.02 -> 1.41e-04 vs 4.06e-02 YES; 0.1 -> 3.51e-03 vs 1.300 YES; 0.5 -> 9.37e-02 vs 2.263e+03 NO (vacuous). The bound goes vacuous precisely when the far field stops being summarisable, which is the formal version of the PSA objection 'mean logits are effective only when logits are nearly uniform'. ROLLBACK: none, it is a diagnostic function with no effect on the kernel path.

text: UTILISATION METHODOLOGY, and why the first measurement was worthless. Using perf_counter with median-of-N, the measured peak swung 6.35 -> 9.41 TFLOP/s between two tests in the same process, which moved the utilisation figure from 40% to 72% with no change to the kernel. Root cause measured: this is a laptop GPU and a 300-GEMM sustained loop runs at 6.70 TFLOP/s against 17.73 in burst. Fixed by using CUDA events with BEST-of-N for both numerator and denominator, which made the peak agree with sigmoid's independently measured 22.1 TFLOP/s on the same part. ANY utilisation number on this class of hardware that does not state its duty cycle is uninterpretable.

text: HONEST COST, both directions. The module is SLOWER than tuned SDPA below 8192 positions (0.06x at 1024) and faster above (7.48x at 32768), and it uses MORE memory at every length measured (1.31x-1.94x). The memory penalty is structural: the pyramid is sum_l N/2^l = 2N entries for each of k and v. sigmoid measured a crossover near 8k-16k for SELECTION-based sparsity on this same GPU; a summarising scheme lands in the same place, so the crossover is a property of the hardware and the sequence length, not of the selection strategy. ROLLBACK for the memory cost: build only the levels a given plan actually references instead of the full ladder, which trims the tail levels; that is untested and I am not claiming it.

text: PART C root cause 1, cross-test contamination: tests/chase/test_stochastic_P.py called torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float64) at MODULE SCOPE. pytest imports every test module during COLLECTION, so it ran before any test did and every other module's torch.eye() came back float64. That is what killed test_kernel_contracts.py::test_residual_path_masks_the_missing_backward with 'expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != double' -- an error with nothing to do with what that test checks. It was COLLECTION-ORDER DEPENDENT, so it appeared and vanished under different -k filters. Fixed in two places: the module now uses a module-scoped autouse fixture, and tests/chase/conftest.py has an autouse fixture that snapshots and restores the default dtype around EVERY test, which covers future callers too. ROLLBACK: drop the conftest fixture and revert the fixture in test_stochastic_P.py; the cost is that any module-scope torch global mutation silently changes unrelated tests.

PART C root cause 2, context poisoning ISOLATED not just documented. tests/chase/conftest.py::run_isolated runs a probe in a fresh interpreter with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1. The two out-of-bounds-schedule probes moved into it and now assert their finding POSITIVELY instead of sitting in the known-red ledger. Measured inside the subprocess: out-of-range offsets -> 'CRASHED RuntimeError Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered' followed by 'CONTEXT_POISONED RuntimeError' on an unrelated torch.randn(8,8).sum() in the same process. Negative block index -> 'NO_EXCEPTION finite=True', i.e. silently plausible garbage, which is worse. Blast radius is now one subprocess instead of 13 tests. ROLLBACK: inline the probes again; the cost is losing 13 unrelated CUDA tests whenever they run.

PART C root cause 3, CPU-only breakage. torch.cuda.is_available() returns True under CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' on torch 2.5.1+cu121 while device_count() is 0, and the next get_device_capability(0) raises 'Invalid device id'. Raised from conftest at import time it took the entire directory down before one test ran. Five modules each had their own skipif built on the same unreliable predicate, so they did not skip on a CPU-only box -- they ran and failed. Fixed once in conftest._has_cuda (is_available AND device_count > 0, wrapped) and all five routed through it. ROLLBACK: revert to torch.cuda.is_available(); the cost is that the suite cannot be run at all by a reader without a GPU, which is the exact reproducibility failure R5's test-order note is about.

PART C mechanism: 37 of the previous failures are FINDINGS, not defects -- the failure message IS the recorded measurement (DEQ losing its fixed point, row-stochastic convex-hull ceiling, top-k has no gradient, floor(20 correct)=floor(20 wrong)=0, the merged kernel's missing backward and NaN row, sm_75 exclusion, the flex_attention adapter gap).
